thread:
Olivia: Heads up — ran into a weird auth/retry jank when upgrading to kotlin-sdk 2.4.0 in the sampleapp on Pixel 8 / Android 14. App freezes for ~1s on 401 recovery path.
Devon: Do you have logs or a repro? Is this Retrofit or raw OkHttp behavior?
Olivia: Minimal repro in sampleapp: using an OkHttp Authenticator that calls our token repo via runBlocking from an Interceptor path. Stack shows main-thread timeouts.
Liam: runBlocking inside an interceptor sounds suspicious. Authenticator should run on network threads but calling suspend code improperly can hop to Main.
Olivia: Exact snippet:
```
class TokenInterceptor : Interceptor {
  override fun intercept(chain: Interceptor.Chain): Response {
    val token = runBlocking { tokenRepo.getToken() }
    return chain.proceed(chain.request().newBuilder().header("Authorization","Bearer $token").build())
  }
}
```
When a 401 comes back, OkHttp triggers the Authenticator which triggers the interceptor path again and we end up doing blocking call that can execute on Dispatchers.Main in sampleapp.
Sanjay: We saw similar but the root cause was the sampleapp's repository using Dispatchers.Main in its coroutines builder (test glue). If your tokenRepo uses withContext(Main) anywhere it will schedule there.
Devon: Two issues: 1) sampleapp mixes coroutine sync blocking inside network hooks; 2) parity confusion — Java examples show synchronous refresh, Kotlin examples encouraged suspend helpers. We need clearer guidance.
Liam: Workarounds: (A) Never call suspend functions via runBlocking on interceptor path; use a synchronous token cache + background refresh queue. (B) If you must block, ensure the token refresh uses Dispatchers.IO and avoid Main.
Olivia: Quick repro steps I used: build sampleapp -> open login flow -> toggle network to slow 3G -> trigger token expiry via test account -> observe UI jank + log spam `java.lang.IllegalStateException: Main dispatcher missing` sometimes.
CI-Bot: CI: failing test linked https://ci/internal/28321 — flaky on emulator API 34.
Devon: I'll open a small PR: update sampleapp TokenRepo to explicitly use withContext(Dispatchers.IO) and add a comment in dev docs: "Don't call suspend token refresh directly from interceptors / authenticators; use synchronous cache or run IO dispatcher." Also add unit test that simulates Authenticator path on main thread.
Sanjay: Also add a note about okhttp Dispatcher and CallTimeout interplay — if you block in interceptor it can starve the dispatcher's queue.
Olivia: Thanks. Small follow-up: should we change the example to show an auth queue pattern (enqueue refresh once + replay requests)? I can draft.
Devon: Yes please — that'll also improve parity across Java/Kotlin samples. PR #1145 opened.
CI-Bot: PR #1145 — sampleapp: token refresh IO-d isolation + docs — awaiting review.
Olivia: :thumbsup: I'll link the repro gist and test app branch in the PR.
